Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's second innings. The two Bangladeshi openers, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam are met with a few verbal volleys from the West Indies fielders. This has not sat well with umpire Kumar Dharmasena, who promptly walks up to West Indies skipper Kraigg Brathwaite for a chat. Ian Bishop, on air, believes that Dharmasena has issued a warning to Brathwaite. Jayden Seales has the new ball in hand. Away we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

As for the West Indies, they began the day in a promising position at 70/1 but endured a dramatic collapse, losing 9 wickets for just 76 runs to be bowled out for 146. Kraigg Brathwaite fought valiantly, as did Keacy Carty, but the rest of the batting lineup offered little resistance. It will be crucial for the hosts to move past this dismal batting display and come out firing with the ball, replicating their strong performance from the first innings. Bangladesh’s batting has yet to truly click in this series, but they will need to rally behind their bowlers, who have secured a slender but vital lead to build upon.

Well, it didn’t take long for Bangladesh to wrap things up after the Lunch break, 18 balls to be precise. Following the disappointment of being bowled out for 164, their bowlers have more than made up for it with a stellar performance. While things didn’t quite go their way with the ball on Day 2, they turned the tide brilliantly this morning and completed the clean-up job after the break. With a maiden Test five-wicket haul, Nahid Rana was the standout in helping the tourists take a slender 18-run lead.

Even after Nahid and Taskin were taken out of the attack, the pressure on the West Indies did not ease. Taijul Islam and Hasan Mahmud combined forces to heap further misery on the hosts. Starting the day at a seemingly comfortable 70/1, the West Indies found themselves in a precarious position as the Bangladeshi bowlers kept chipping away with a spirited and disciplined display. Trailing by 29 runs with just two wickets in hand, the hosts are scrambling to avoid conceding a lead on a wicket where you are never really in as a batter. It was a dramatic first session and the second session promises to bring even more drama. See you shortly for the continuation of this intriguing contest!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to commence on Day 3. Glorious sunshine greets the two umpires and players as they make their way out to the middle.  Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Taijul Islam. Taijul to Carty first up. Let's play...

Bangladesh's head coach, Phil Simmons is in for a chat. He says that the sun was out for a long time on the opening day and due to the late start, they felt that batting first was the way to go. Adds that they wanted to put West Indies under pressure with runs on the board. Talking about the the batting, he says that patience is key and they will have to do better in the second innings. Feels that they will have to be consistent in hitting the good areas with the ball on Day 3.

PITCH REPORT - Nikhil Uttamchandani is near the deck. He notes that all 11 wickets have fallen so far to pacers, which isn't surprising given the history of the venue and the green tinge on the surface. Samuel Badree joins him and mentions that as the game progresses, spinners are likely to have a bigger impact. He highlights that the end where Taijul Islam bowled on Day 2 will continue to assist spinners, especially with the bare patches that have developed. Mentions that at the other end, fissures are increasing, which will lead to more sideways movement and uneven bounce, making it trickier for the batters as the day progresses.

Bangladesh will need to regroup and put up a strong performance after a disappointing Day 2. Despite a solid start with the bat, they could not capitalise, succumbing to the pressure from West Indies' seamers. Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan will be crucial if Bangladesh are to bounce back, as they look to extract turn and bounce on offer and make life difficult for the West Indies' batters. Their fielding woes continued as Mehidy dropped a crucial chance late in the day, letting Brathwaite off the hook. The visitors will have to dig deep to stay competitive in this match. We started early on Day 2 to compensate for the time lost on the opening day, and that will be the case today as well. The first ball will be bowled at 2.45 pm GMT, so stay tuned!

For West Indies, Day 2 was dominated by Jayden Seales' spectacular bowling performance. His 4-wicket haul dismantled Bangladesh and bowled them out for 164. Alongside him, Shamar Joseph also delivered a strong spell, contributing to Bangladesh’s collapse. Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty held firm with the bat, reaching stumps at 70/1, with Brathwaite staying unbeaten on 33. Trailing by 94 runs, the hosts will be eager to start well and then take it from there as they look to take the lead.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of the 2nd Test match between the West Indies and Bangladesh! After a gripping Day 2, all eyes will be on the pitch at Sabina Park as both teams aim to take control. We saw some turn and bounce late on Day 2 when Taijul Islam started operating from one end, giving indications that there is enough for everyone on this pitch. We might see a lot more turn on Day 3 with the cracks expected to widen, making it trickier for the batters as the match progresses. There is a slight chance of an isolated shower later in the day, which might interrupt play, but let's hope for the best.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Bangladesh have made the West Indies work hard for every single run, and they will aim to maintain the same intensity with the ball on Day 3. The spinners have extracted considerable turn, while the pacers remained effective even as the ball aged. The hosts, trailing by 94 runs, will look to steadily reduce the deficit and take a sizable lead. A solid start on Day 3 will be critical to setting a strong foundation and asserting control over the game. It’s all set up for an intriguing day of Test cricket. It will be yet another early start with the first ball on Day 3 to be bowled at 2.45 pm GMT. As always, you can join us earlier for the build-up. See you then. Cheers!

Shamar Joseph comes in for a quick chat. He says that they come out as a bowling group wanting to do the best for the team. Further adds that he wants to stick to the basics and bowl as straight as possible. Mentions that he wants to bowl as fast as possible and that's what keeps him happy. Concludes that being amongst the wickets keeps him happy as well.

In reply, the Bangladeshi pacers matched the discipline shown by their West Indies counterparts, while Taijul Islam’s quality spin added to the challenges for the hosts' top order. Run-scoring proved difficult, and a rash shot from Mikyle Louis resulted in his early dismissal. Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty then steadied the innings, digging in to consolidate the West Indies' position. Brathwaite, in particular, looked uncertain against Taijul, surviving a few nervy moments, including a dropped catch when he was on 26. Meanwhile, Carty battled through his own struggles, showing grit despite dealing with discomfort in his lower back.

Earlier in the day, Bangladesh resumed at 69/2 as Shahadat Hossain and Shadman Islam held their ground well, building on their solid start from the truncated opening day. However, Shamar Joseph played a key role in breaking through, and with Jayden Seales by his side, the West Indies quickly made further inroads. From 83/2, Bangladesh slipped to 98/6 in no time. Mehidy Hasan showed resilience, standing firm alongside Taijul Islam and Taskin Ahmed, but the relentless short-ball tactic from the West Indies eventually saw the downfall of all three. Jayden Seales, who had bowled well without much reward earlier in the innings, ended up with remarkable figures of 15.5-10-5-4 as the Windies rolled Bangladesh over for 164.

It got gloomier in the last few overs of the second session, prompting the floodlights to be switched on. With 44 overs remaining in the day, it looks unlikely that we all get through all of them, as bad light could bring an abrupt end to play. The Bangladeshi pacers will hope for better fortunes in the third session, but the key for them will be to remain patient and maintain consistent pressure. They will need to test the West Indies openers, who have shown some vulnerability, and hope that the conditions bring opportunities their way. Back in a bit for the third session.

In reply, Mikyle Louis and Kraigg Brathwaite managed to navigate through a tricky passage of play before the Tea break, although they were not without their nervy moments. Hasan Mahmud and Taskin Ahmed were disciplined in their approach, testing both openers with probing lines, but the two West Indies' openers had just enough fortune to survive.

SESSION SUMMARY - 23.5 overs, 58 runs and 4 wickets. Another session dominated by the West Indies! As play resumed after the Lunch break, Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam continued to resist. However, the hosts' relentless short-ball strategy soon paid off. Taijul fell first, and with little support from the other end, Mehidy also fell while trying to counter the barrage of short deliveries. From 83/2, Bangladesh lost their last 8 wickets for just 81 runs, being bowled out for 164.
